scientific_hypothesis: A dual-cavity defect structure using high-index Ge and low-index YbF3 can simultaneously transmit two narrow bands (3.25-3.35 μm and 4.20-4.30 μm) while blocking adjacent regions, with cavity positions and thicknesses optimized under TMM.
expected_advantages: High index contrast (Ge ~4.0, YbF3 ~1.5) enables strong blocking with fewer layers
Dual-cavity design naturally supports two independent passbands
known_risks: Ge has absorption in mid-IR that may reduce peak transmittance
Cavity coupling may cause passband interaction if spacing is incorrect
Previous route_03 failed due to layer count mismatch - this route explicitly declares 22 layers
expected_observations: best_target_score should show improvement in blocking bands if additional layers help
tightest_margin may decrease if transmission drops in passbands
valid_candidates count should remain positive if 24-layer constraint is feasible
If hypothesis is false: best_target_score will not improve despite additional layers, indicating 22-layer is near-optimal
stop_conditions: If best_target_score improvement relative to route_02 is < 1e-3 for 2 consecutive rounds, judge additional layers as not beneficial -> stop and prefer 22-layer design
If valid_candidates = 0, judge 24-layer constraint set as infeasible -> revert to 22-layer topology
